title: Miyan Zogale
author: Dobby Eghosa
desc: The only northern soup in the record with its water quantified — half a cup of raw groundnut to a litre and a half — finished when there is oil at the top.
longDesc: Miyan zogale is moringa leaf soup and it is the one northern soup where a named source actually states the liquid volume: a litre and a half of water to half a cup of raw shelled groundnut. Everything else in the northern repertoire leaves the denominator blank. Half a kilo of meat, a dried fish, two large bunches of moringa, a tablespoon of yaji, a teaspoon of kaun and half a flat of daddawa go in alongside, with two cooking spoons of palm oil. It takes over an hour, and the finishing cue is straightforward — there will be oil at the top when it is done.
equipment: Dry pan, for roasting the groundnuts
steps: Pick and wash the moringa leaves thoroughly.
Prepare the other ingredients — chop the onion, blend the tomatoes and peppers, grind the daddawa.
Roast the groundnuts in a dry pan, then grind them to a paste.
Cook the meat and dried fish with the seasoning cubes, onion and salt.
Heat the palm oil and stir-fry the blended tomatoes and peppers.
Add the meat and its stock, the groundnut paste, the yaji, the daddawa and the kaun, with the water, and cook through.
Add the moringa leaves and simmer 3 minutes.
It is done when there is oil at the top of the soup.
chefTips: Half a cup of groundnut to a litre and a half of water. That is the only stated liquid volume in any northern Nigerian soup in this collection, and it is worth having for scaling anything else.
Oil at the top is the doneness cue, and it is the same signal that finishes most Nigerian soups built on a fried pepper base.
Roast the groundnuts before grinding. Raw groundnut paste tastes green and chalky.
Three minutes on the leaves. Another named source gives ten — a large difference in final texture for a leaf as tender as moringa, and three is the shorter and greener of the two.
A teaspoon of kaun. See NGA120 for what this actually is chemically and for the safety note that belongs with it.
Yaji in a soup rather than on meat. A tablespoon gives the whole pot the suya-spice character, which is distinctively northern.
Wash the moringa thoroughly. The leaves are small and sandy and there is no fixing it later.
commonMistakes: Cooking the moringa for ten minutes when three is enough.
Adding the kaun by eye rather than measuring the teaspoon.
Skipping the stir-fry of the tomato and pepper base.
sources: Adapted from 'Miyan Zogale - Moringa Soup', Dobby's Signature — no author explicitly named on the page beyond the blog name, so credited to the site. Local names as printed: Miyan Zogale; 'Zogale' is Hausa for moringa leaves. Prep time as printed: 15 minutes. Cook time as printed: 'Over an hour'.

Quantities exactly as printed: 1/2 kg Meat; 1 medium-sized dried fish; 2 Large bunch Zogale (Moringa leaves); 3 Large size fresh tomatoes; 3 medium-sized fresh pepper; 1 medium size Onion; 1 tbsp. Yaji; 1/2 cup Gyada (Raw Shelled Groundnut); 1 tsp. Kaun (potash); 1 1/2 litres Water; 1/2 flat Daddawa; 2 cooking spoon palm oil; 3 seasoning cubes; salt to taste.

THIS IS THE ONLY NORTHERN SOUP IN THIS COLLECTION WITH A STATED LIQUID VOLUME — 1.5 litres — which makes the groundnut-to-water ratio of 1/2 cup : 1.5 L the only one derivable in the northern set. Miyan kuka, by contrast, quantifies its thickener and never its liquid (NGA087).

The method on the page runs as six sequential steps covering leaf preparation, ingredient prep, groundnut roasting, meat and fish cooking, oil-based stir-frying, and final assembly with a 3-minute simmer. Serving as printed: 'Serve with Tuwo shinkafa, tuwo masara, Burabisko or any form of "swallow"'. Yield not specified.

THE DONENESS CUE is from the second named source and it is the better one: Daily Trust, 'How to prepare Moringa Soup (Miyan zogale)', byline 'ByNana Yusuf' — 'There will be oil at the top of the soup when it is done.'

THAT SECOND SOURCE GIVES NO QUANTITIES FOR ANY INGREDIENT, and it has a printed defect worth recording: its opening ingredient line is truncated mid-phrase in the published article, reading 'Ground dried' and stopping. That has not been guessed at. Its method also contains an internal contradiction — step 4 says to add all other ingredients EXCEPT the groundnut paste, then step 5 immediately adds the groundnut paste, making the exclusion pointless as written.
DISAGREEMENT ON THE LEAF SIMMER, not reconciled: 3 minutes here against 10 minutes in the Daily Trust version. For a leaf as tender as moringa that is a large difference in final texture.
For what kaun actually is — chemically trona, a sodium mineral, not potassium carbonate — and for the safety note that belongs beside any recipe calling for it, see NGA120.
reheating: Low heat with a splash of water.
healthBenefits: Moringa leaf is exceptionally high in vitamin A, vitamin C, calcium and protein for a vegetable.
Groundnut adds plant protein and niacin.
Red palm oil supplies carotenoids and vitamin E.
High in protein from the meat and dried fish.
culturalNote: Zogale is moringa, the tree that grows almost anywhere in the north and whose leaves are among the most nutrient-dense foods on the continent. That it is cooked into a soup with groundnut and daddawa rather than treated as a health supplement is the point — it has been an ordinary vegetable in northern Nigeria for far longer than it has been a superfood anywhere else.
